title: EOS Analytics and KPI Specification
description: What EOS measures and displays — business intelligence for founders: KPI framework, dashboard metrics, AI insights, reporting, benchmarking, and agent performance analytics
provenance_detail: Analytics not specified in PRD beyond 'KPI strip' on the home dashboard. This artifact infers the full analytics and KPI system required for a production business-in-a-box operating system, drawing from the ontology (portfolio/entity/business hierarchy), agent architecture (10 agents, 9 departments), UI/UX canon (executive command center aesthetic), and communication/delegation architecture. Every metric traces to the EOS hierarchy: Operator -> Portfolio -> Entity -> Business Operations -> Teams/Agents -> Workflows/Tasks -> Capital/KPIs -> Outcomes.

analytics_platform.rationale: PostHog provides product analytics, session replay, feature flags, and experimentation in a single self-hostable platform. Aligns with UMH self-sovereignty principle — no vendor lock-in on business intelligence.

integration_model.client_side: PostHog JS SDK in React shell for UI event tracking, session replay, feature flags
integration_model.server_side: PostHog Python SDK for agent execution events, workflow completions, API-level metrics
integration_model.data_warehouse: Neon Postgres as primary store, PostHog as analytics overlay — not a replacement for the transactional database

analytics_platform.alternative_considered: Custom analytics on Neon Postgres with materialized views. PostHog preferred for session replay, funnel analysis, and experimentation features that would be expensive to build custom.

kpi_framework.design_principle: Every KPI must be actionable, attributable to a hierarchy level, and measurable without manual data entry. If the system cannot compute it from transactional data, it is not a KPI — it is a vanity metric.

dashboard_metrics.design_principle: Progressive disclosure. Home dashboard shows the 5-8 numbers that matter most. Drill-down reveals department, entity, and historical detail. Never overwhelm. Finance-grade clarity, not dashboard-porn.

home_dashboard.description: The KPI strip visible immediately on login. Executive summary — the numbers a founder checks first thing in the morning.
home_dashboard.customization: Operator can pin/unpin metrics, reorder strip, change comparison period. Persisted per-operator in preferences.

portfolio_view.description: Consolidated analytics across all entities in a portfolio. Comparative view — see which entities outperform, which need attention.

entity_detail.description: Deep-dive into a single entity. All universal KPIs plus entity-type-specific KPIs. Department breakdown.

sections.name: entity_type_specific_kpis
sections.description: Renders additional KPIs from per_entity_type_kpis based on this entity's type

department_view.description: Per-department analytics page. Shows department-specific KPIs, agent performance, workflow status, and task pipeline.

real_time_vs_batch.design_principle: Real-time where the operator needs to act now. Batch where historical aggregation produces better signal. Never pay the cost of real-time for metrics that only matter weekly.

real_time_metrics.description: Updated on every relevant transaction or event. Pushed via WebSocket to connected clients.
real_time_metrics.implementation_note: Real-time metrics require event-driven computation. Each transaction/event triggers a recalculation of affected metrics. Use Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY for change propagation, or application-level event bus.

daily_batch_metrics.description: Computed once per day during overnight batch job. Historical aggregation that benefits from full-day data.

weekly_batch_metrics.description: Metrics that require weekly aggregation for meaningful signal. Computed on Monday 0300 UTC.

ai_insights.design_principle: AI augments the numbers with meaning. Every insight must be actionable — 'revenue dropped 12%' is not an insight; 'revenue dropped 12% because enterprise deal X slipped — Sales Agent recommends rescheduling the demo' is an insight. Deterministic detection first, AI narration second.

next_best_action.description: AI-generated recommended actions surfaced on the home dashboard and in the EA Agent's morning brief. Always backed by data, always attributable to a specific metric or trend.

format.headline: One-sentence action recommendation
format.rationale: Why this action matters, grounded in data
format.metric_context: Which KPI(s) this relates to, with current values
format.suggested_agent: Which department agent should handle this
format.estimated_impact: Quantified expected outcome if action is taken

anomaly_detection.description: Automatic detection of unusual patterns in KPI data. Deterministic rules for known patterns, statistical methods for unknown patterns.

detection_methods.name: threshold_breach
detection_methods.description: Metric crosses operator-defined threshold (e.g., runway < 3 months)

detection_methods.name: percentage_deviation
detection_methods.description: Metric deviates more than N% from trailing average (e.g., daily revenue drops 30% vs trailing 7-day average)

detection_methods.name: trend_break
detection_methods.description: Metric trend reverses direction after sustained movement (e.g., MRR was growing 5% MoM for 6 months, now flat)

detection_methods.name: seasonal_anomaly
detection_methods.description: Metric deviates from expected seasonal pattern

alert_routing.critical: Push notification to operator + EA Agent morning brief + dashboard alert banner
alert_routing.high: EA Agent morning brief + dashboard alert badge
alert_routing.medium: Dashboard alert badge + department view notification

trend_analysis.description: AI-narrated trend reports that contextualize KPI movements over time. Provides the 'so what' behind the numbers.

components.name: momentum_indicator
components.description: For each KPI: accelerating, decelerating, stable, or reversing. Deterministic calculation.

components.name: correlation_detection
components.description: Identify when two KPIs move together unexpectedly (e.g., marketing spend up but CAC also up — diminishing returns)

components.name: narrative_summary
components.description: LLM-generated plain-English summary of trends for the morning brief
components.fallback: Template-based summary using metric values and direction labels

forecasting.description: Forward-looking projections for key financial and operational metrics. Always displayed with confidence intervals. Deterministic baseline, AI-enhanced where data supports it.

models.name: linear_projection
models.description: Simple linear extrapolation from trailing data. Always available as baseline.

models.name: cohort_based_revenue_forecast
models.description: Revenue forecast based on existing customer cohort behavior + pipeline conversion rates

models.name: ai_enhanced_forecast
models.description: LLM adjusts statistical forecast based on contextual factors (market conditions, planned campaigns, known deal movements)

reporting.design_principle: Reports are for communication and record-keeping. Dashboards are for real-time awareness. Never make the operator build a report manually — the system produces them on schedule or on demand.

scheduled_reports.name: morning_brief
scheduled_reports.description: Daily executive summary delivered via EA Agent. KPI snapshot, anomalies, next best actions, today's agenda.

scheduled_reports.name: weekly_business_review
scheduled_reports.description: Weekly rollup of all KPIs with week-over-week comparison, trend narratives, and department highlights.

scheduled_reports.name: monthly_financial_report
scheduled_reports.description: Monthly P&L, cash flow statement, balance sheet summary, and financial KPI analysis.

scheduled_reports.name: quarterly_strategic_review
scheduled_reports.description: Quarterly deep-dive with OKR progress, competitive analysis, and strategic recommendations from CEO Agent.

ad_hoc.description: Operator can request any report via EA Agent natural language. 'Give me a sales report for Q1' or 'How did marketing perform last month?'
ad_hoc.mechanism: EA Agent parses intent, routes to appropriate department agent, agent compiles report from available data, returns formatted output.
supported_queries: customer analysis (top customers, churn risk, LTV distribution)

export_formats.description: Branded PDF with charts and tables. Primary output format for formal reports.
Raw data export for any metric or report table. For spreadsheet analysis.
Structured data export for API consumers or integrations.
Excel workbook with multiple sheets for complex reports. Includes formulas where applicable.

benchmarking.design_principle: A number without context is noise. Benchmarking provides the context: 'Your churn rate is 5%' means nothing; 'Your churn rate is 5% vs 3% industry median for SaaS at your stage' drives action.

cross_entity.description: Compare entities within the same portfolio on shared KPIs. Which of your businesses is most capital-efficient? Which has the longest runway?
cross_entity.implementation: Rank entities on each universal KPI. Display as comparison table with color-coded quartiles.

cross_portfolio.description: Compare portfolios against each other on aggregate KPIs. For operators with multiple portfolios.
cross_portfolio.implementation: Aggregate universal KPIs per portfolio. Display as side-by-side comparison.

industry_benchmarks.description: Compare entity KPIs against industry/stage benchmarks. Requires external benchmark data source.

data_sources.name: static_benchmark_tables
data_sources.description: Curated benchmark data compiled from public sources (SaaS benchmarks from OpenView, Bessemer; agency benchmarks from Promethean Research; etc.)

data_sources.name: anonymous_aggregate
data_sources.description: If EOS achieves sufficient user base, anonymous cross-platform benchmarks from opt-in users

display.example: Your CAC is $47 (25th percentile for early-stage SaaS — better than 75% of peers)

industry_benchmarks.provenance_note: Industry benchmarks are INFERRED_PROFESSIONAL_GAP — the PRD does not specify benchmarking. This is standard in any serious business analytics platform.

agent_performance.design_principle: Agents are employees. They get performance reviews. Every agent's effectiveness is measured, tracked, and visible to the operator. This is how the operator trusts (or revokes trust from) AI autonomy.

per_agent_metrics.description: Standardized performance metrics tracked for every agent in the system.

metrics.name: average_task_duration
metrics.label: Avg Task Duration
metrics.description: Mean time from task assignment to completion

metrics.name: escalation_rate
metrics.label: Escalation Rate
metrics.description: Tasks escalated to human / total tasks. High escalation means the agent cannot handle its domain.

metrics.name: autonomous_completion_rate
metrics.label: Autonomous Completion Rate
metrics.description: Tasks completed without any human intervention / total tasks

metrics.name: error_rate
metrics.label: Error Rate
metrics.description: Tasks resulting in error or requiring correction / total tasks

metrics.name: cost_per_task
metrics.label: Cost Per Task
metrics.description: LLM API cost + compute cost per task. The economic efficiency of the agent.

metrics.name: quality_score
metrics.label: Quality Score
metrics.description: Composite quality score based on output accuracy, completeness, and operator feedback. 0-100 scale.

metrics.name: improvement_trend
metrics.label: Improvement Trend
metrics.description: Is this agent getting better or worse over time? Based on quality score trailing average.

metrics.name: permission_tier_utilization
metrics.label: Permission Tier Utilization
metrics.description: How often the agent operates at its maximum permission tier. High utilization on COMMIT-tier agents may indicate risk.

task_completion_tracking.description: Every task assigned to an agent is tracked from assignment to resolution with full audit trail.
tracked_fields: status (queued, in_progress, completed, failed, escalated, cancelled)
task_completion_tracking.retention: indefinite — task history is the foundation of agent improvement

quality_scoring.description: Multi-dimensional quality assessment for agent outputs. Deterministic checks first, operator feedback as calibration.

dimensions.name: accuracy
dimensions.description: Did the agent produce correct output? For deterministic tasks: exact match. For generative tasks: factual accuracy against source data.

dimensions.name: completeness
dimensions.description: Did the agent address all aspects of the task? Measured by checklist completion for structured tasks.

dimensions.name: timeliness
dimensions.description: Did the agent complete within expected timeframe?
dimensions.measurement: actual_duration / expected_duration (capped at 1.0 for early completion)

dimensions.name: operator_satisfaction
dimensions.description: Explicit operator feedback (thumbs up/down, rating, correction). Most valuable signal but sparsest.

quality_scoring.recalibration: Weights adjustable per-operator. Some founders care more about speed, others about accuracy.

agent_dashboard.description: Dedicated view for monitoring all agent performance. Accessible from the operations department view or directly from the nav rail.

sections.name: agent_detail
sections: task_history_table (recent 50 tasks with status and outcome)
cost_breakdown (LLM costs, compute costs, per task and total)
permission_audit (actions taken at each permission tier)

mvp_scope.description: Which analytics capabilities ship in which EOS release. Progressive build-out — not everything at once.

r1_core_shell.notes: R1 establishes the KPI strip pattern. 5 metrics, no drill-down, no benchmarking.

r3_finance_ops.notes: R3 is where analytics becomes serious. Financial reporting is the backbone.

r5_docs_memory.notes: R5 is the full analytics platform. AI insights and benchmarking go live.

data_architecture.description: How KPI data flows from source to dashboard.

computation_layer.real_time: Application-level event handlers compute and cache real-time metrics on each transaction. Redis or in-memory cache for sub-second reads.
computation_layer.batch: Scheduled jobs query Neon, compute aggregate metrics, write results to a kpi_snapshots table. Dashboards read from snapshots, not raw transactions.

kpi_snapshots.note: Immutable append-only. Historical snapshots never updated — new row per computation.

caching_strategy.hot_metrics: Redis/in-memory for real-time KPIs. TTL = 0 (invalidated on event).
caching_strategy.dashboard_cache: Pre-computed dashboard payloads cached per operator+entity. TTL = 5 minutes for non-real-time views.
caching_strategy.report_cache: Generated reports cached as files. Invalidated on next batch computation.

open_questions.question: PostHog vs custom analytics stack? PostHog adds session replay and experimentation but is another dependency. Custom on Neon is simpler but requires building charting, funnels, and cohort analysis.
open_questions.recommendation: Use PostHog for product analytics (user behavior, session replay, feature flags) and custom Neon for business KPIs (financial metrics, agent performance). Two complementary systems, not one replacing the other.

open_questions.question: Should EOS support custom metric definitions by the operator, or are the pre-defined KPIs sufficient?
open_questions.recommendation: Pre-defined KPIs for MVP. Custom metric builder is a post-scale feature — the complexity of a formula builder is not worth it until operators are asking for it.

open_questions.question: What are the authoritative benchmark data sources for each entity type? SaaS has well-known benchmarks (OpenView, Bessemer). Agency, real estate, and content businesses have fewer standardized sources.
open_questions.recommendation: Start with SaaS benchmarks only (most mature, most relevant to initial user base). Add other entity types as user demand materializes.

open_questions.question: How does the analytics system handle multi-currency entities within a single portfolio?
open_questions.recommendation: All financial KPIs stored in native currency with a normalized USD equivalent. Portfolio-level aggregation uses USD normalization. Exchange rates updated daily from a free API (exchangerate-api or similar).

open_questions.question: What is the data retention policy for KPI snapshots? Indefinite storage grows linearly with entity count and metric count.
open_questions.recommendation: Full daily resolution for 2 years, weekly rollups for years 3-5, monthly rollups beyond 5 years. Retention policy configurable per operator.

open_questions.question: Should agent cost tracking include only LLM API costs or also imputed compute/infrastructure costs?
open_questions.recommendation: LLM API costs are directly attributable and should be tracked from day one. Infrastructure costs are shared and should be allocated proportionally only when the system is at scale.
